title: You thought your story was already decided.
paragraphs:
You thought your story was already decided.
The mistakes. The nights no one saw. The quiet guilt that follows you even when everything looks fine on the outside.
But listen—this will shake you if you let it.
Your ending has already been claimed… by Someone stronger than your past.
“I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, “who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty.” (Revelation 1:8)

Not “I was.”
Not “I might be.”
Not “I’m trying to fix things.”
I AM.

Alpha.
The beginning.

Omega.
The end.

That means before your first breath—He was already there.
And long after your last heartbeat—He will still be God.
So why are you living like everything depends on you?
Why are you carrying a weight you were never meant to hold?
Some of you are exhausted… not because life is heavy—but because you’re trying to be your own Alpha and Omega.

You’re trying to start your own healing.
You’re trying to control your own outcome.
You’re trying to rewrite your own story.
And it’s breaking you.
Because only God can stand at both ends of time and say, “I hold it all together.”
Here’s the truth most people avoid:
Sin makes us forget who is really in control.

It whispers lies like—
“You’ve gone too far.”
“You’ve ruined everything.”
“There’s no coming back from this.”
But the Gospel answers louder.

The Alpha stepped into our broken beginning.
The Omega stepped into our deserved ending.
Jesus Christ—fully God, fully man—entered time, took on flesh, and walked into our mess without flinching. He didn’t avoid sinners. He moved toward them.

Toward liars.
Toward addicts.
Toward the ashamed.
Toward the ones hiding behind curated lives and silent regrets.
And then the unthinkable happened.
He took the weight of sin—your sin, my sin—upon Himself.
At the cross, it looked like the end.

Darkness.
Blood.
Silence.
Hope seemed buried.
But three days later—
The Omega rewrote the ending.

The tomb opened.
Death lost its grip.
Jesus rose—not as a symbol—but as a living, victorious Savior.
And that changes everything.
Because now, the One who holds the end… offers you a new beginning.
Let that sink in.

Your failure is not final.
Your shame is not sovereign.
Your past is not your master.
Jesus is.
And He doesn’t just observe your story—He redeems it.
Some scholars interpret Revelation 1:8 as both a declaration of God’s eternal nature and a direct affirmation of Christ’s divine authority. Either way, the message stands unshaken:
The One who began all things will also bring them to completion.
So if you are in Christ, your life is not spiraling—it is being shaped.

Even the pain.
Even the delay.
Even the seasons that make no sense.

He is Alpha there.
He is Omega there.
Which means—

There is purpose in your waiting.
There is mercy in your correction.
There is hope beyond what you can currently see.
But don’t miss this:

Grace is not automatic.
It is received.

Not earned.
Not performed for.
Not negotiated.
Received through repentance and faith in Jesus alone.

Turn from sin.
Trust in Christ.
Surrender the illusion of control.
Because the same voice that spoke galaxies into existence is calling your name.

Not to condemn you—
but to restore you.

Not to shame you—
but to save you.

Not to end you—
but to begin something brand new.
So here’s the question you can’t ignore:
Who is writing your story right now?

Is it your fear?
Your past?
Your addiction?
Your pride?
Or have you finally surrendered the pen to the Alpha and Omega?
Because one day—every story reaches its final page.
And only one ending leads to life.
Jesus Christ. Crucified. Risen. Reigning.

This is not religion.
This is rescue.
And it’s still available—right now.

Come back.
Even if you feel far.

Come home.
Even if you feel unworthy.

Come to Jesus.
Because the beginning and the end are not against you—
If you belong to Him.

Your story is not over.
It’s being rewritten.
Type “ALPHA & OMEGA” if you believe Jesus holds your story.
Because it’s not.

Not while He is still the Alpha…
and the Omega.
